newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Twenty lives lost needlessly after a Greek ship capsized in the Aegean over the weekend. The blame for the accident has been placed on bad organisation, bad weather and the delayed reaction on the part of naval and merchant marine ministry services. The ministry blames the captain of the vessel for sailing in bad weather.
--The lone survivor of the weekend's tragic accident describes his miraculous escape. Divers had recovered eight bodies by early this morning and hopes of survivors were fading.

--Athens Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos leading the field in a new poll on who is best suited to lead the conservative opposition New Democracy party with 29.9 percent. Incumbent Miltiades Evert and hopeful George Souflias are neck and neck at 12.4 percent.

--There are questions about the state's delayed response to the capsizing of the "Dystos" - rescue services reached the ailing vessel three nautical miles off the island of Evia nine hours after receiving the SOS signal.
--Lone survivor Christos Anagnostou says he was sure the ship would capsize.
